holidays.name: National Junk Food Day
holidays.description: A day to guiltlessly embrace chips, candy, soda, and every gloriously greasy snack your pantry has been hiding. Nutrition labels are politely asked to look the other way.
holidays.origin: Like many unofficial food holidays, it grew out of grassroots food-calendar culture and snack lovers online, with no single known founder. It has been observed on July 21 in the United States for years.
holidays.funFact: The term 'junk food' is often credited to Michael Jacobson of the Center for Science in the Public Interest, who popularized it in the early 1970s.

holidays.name: National Ice Cream Day Weekend Wind-Down (Third Sunday Aftermath)
holidays.description: Not an official holiday, but July 21 often falls near National Ice Cream Day, so people extend the celebration with leftover scoops, sprinkles, and brain freezes.
holidays.origin: In 1984, President Ronald Reagan designated July as National Ice Cream Month and the third Sunday of July as National Ice Cream Day. The date shifts each year, so this unofficial wind-down sometimes lands on July 21.
holidays.funFact: Reagan's proclamation encouraged Americans to observe the occasion 'with appropriate ceremonies and activities,' which is an excellent excuse for sundaes.

holidays.name: Hemingway Days (Key West Celebration)
holidays.description: Key West, Florida, hosts a week of festivities honoring author Ernest Hemingway, featuring a famous look-alike contest where bearded, white-haired men compete to be 'Papa.'
holidays.origin: Hemingway Days began in 1981 and is held around his birthday, July 21, 1899. Key West was one of Hemingway's homes in the 1930s.
holidays.funFact: The Hemingway look-alike contest draws well over 100 contestants some years, and the house where he lived is famous for its many six-toed cats.

holidays.name: Fry Day Fan Celebration: National Daiquiri Day Neighbor
holidays.description: Many cocktail fans toast the daiquiri around this time of year, and July 21 is a popular unofficial day for raising a frosty glass of rum, lime, and sugar.
holidays.origin: The daiquiri is traditionally linked to Cuba and an American engineer named Jennings Cox, who is said to have created it around 1898 near the town of Daiquirí. Observances of its day vary, with July 19 the most common date.
holidays.funFact: Ernest Hemingway was a famous daiquiri fan and reportedly favored a sugar-free version with extra rum, which became known as the 'Papa Doble.'

holidays.name: Moon Landing Week Celebration: Lunar Legacy Day
holidays.description: On July 21, 1969, Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin were making history on the Moon in UTC terms, and space nerds mark the day with moon pies, astronaut ice cream, and Moon-themed trivia.
holidays.origin: Apollo 11 landed on July 20, 1969, but Armstrong first stepped onto the surface early on July 21 UTC, so many around the world observe the moonwalk date on July 21.
holidays.funFact: Armstrong's first step took place at 02:56 UTC on July 21, 1969, and an estimated 600 million people watched it live.
